findings.title: Resource leak: opened file not closed
findings.body: The file opened on line 7 is appended to `_open_reports` but never closed, causing a resource leak. The original code used a context manager (`with`) to ensure the file was closed immediately after reading. The new code breaks this invariant by keeping the file open in a global list.
findings.suggestion:
with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as report:
        return report.read()

findings.title: Global mutable list `_open_reports` lacks thread-safety and purpose
findings.body: The global list `_open_reports` is mutable and lacks any synchronization, making it unsafe in multi-threaded contexts. Its purpose is unclear: it is neither documented nor used elsewhere in the diff. This violates the Clean Architecture rule that business logic should not leak into global state or entrypoints.

summary.problem: The change introduces a resource leak and a global mutable list, breaking correctness and architectural boundaries.
summary.done_well: The refactor attempts to avoid closing the file immediately, though the intent is unclear.
